rubrics.justification: The model explicitly stated that no image was available to it and did not fabricate embryo morphology. It only described general features it would assess, which avoids inaccurate claims.

It integrated age, ovarian reserve, oocyte maturity, endometrial thickness, diagnosis, sperm data, BMI, and cycle history into prognosis well, though interaction with actual embryo morphology was necessarily limited by lack of image access.

The reasoning is logical and internally consistent, with prognosis appropriately broadened because morphology was unavailable. Minor limitation: implantation ranges are somewhat generic and not tightly anchored to the visible embryo.

Recommendations are broadly consistent with IVF practice: preference for single embryo transfer in a young good-prognosis patient, no routine PGT-A, attention to luteal support and review of fertilization/blastulation data. Slightly limited by generic rather than guideline-cited nuance.

Provides practical next steps for current transfer and future review, including SET, luteal support, nutritional optimization, and what additional lab data to assess if unsuccessful. Useful, though not highly tailored to the actual embryo morphology.
